title: Reverse a list
summary: Three pointers flip one arrow per round.

checkpoints.text: `prev` is the part already reversed (empty so far), `cur` is the node being worked on, `next` will remember the rest of the list.
Save the rest of the list first. After the next line, `cur->next` will no longer lead there.
The arrow of the first node is turned around. It now points at `prev`, which is NULL, so this node will be the new end.
`prev` and `cur` both step one node to the right. One arrow has been flipped.
Second round, second arrow. The boxes never move; only the arrows change direction.
`cur` ran off the end, and `prev` points at the old last node, which is the new first node. That is why `prev` is returned.
